work.title: STILLWATER
work.subtitle: 共享阅读角概念提案书
work.framework: proposal: Condition for discussion / distinct native A4 document layout
work.scope: Fictional shared-reading concept. No venue permission, dimensions, procurement quote, construction specification or accessibility approval.

pages.title: Propose a conversation, not a finished room.
pages.lead: STILLWATER explores an imagined shared reading corner as a proposal for discussion. Its scenes establish visual tone, not a real site or approved design.
pages.body: The proposal asks whether a small reading-focused setting is worth investigating. It does not claim that a venue, budget, operator or responsible reviewer has been appointed.
pages.detail: Use this section to record a bounded response to the question below. Retain the distinction between the fictional example, your interpretation and any separate evidence a real use would require.
pages.question: State the decision this discussion could responsibly inform.

pages.title: Use the proposal in three passes.
pages.lead: First read the intention, then the unresolved conditions, then the proposed handoff. A persuasive image should not hide a missing source.
pages.body: Pages 3–5 explain the idea and alternatives. Pages 6–8 distinguish responsibilities, resources and review questions. Pages 9–10 identify the response sought and the limits of the proposal.
pages.detail: Use this section to record a bounded response to the question below. Retain the distinction between the fictional example, your interpretation and any separate evidence a real use would require.
pages.question: Choose a question for each reading pass.

pages.title: Define the problem without inventing demand.
pages.lead: The imagined issue is a desire for a quieter place to read together. That desire is a premise for the exercise, not a measured community need.
pages.body: A real problem statement would identify its source and scope. Until such evidence exists, use language such as intention to explore rather than unmet demand has been proven.
pages.detail: Use this section to record a bounded response to the question below. Retain the distinction between the fictional example, your interpretation and any separate evidence a real use would require.
pages.question: Which source would establish a real need?

pages.title: Describe the proposed experience.
pages.lead: Imagine arriving, finding a place to pause and choosing whether to read alone or join a conversation. This narrative is not a tested user journey.
pages.body: The sequence helps a reader discuss atmosphere and purpose. It does not supply an approved route, furniture arrangement, capacity or rule for operating a real space.
pages.detail: Use this section to record a bounded response to the question below. Retain the distinction between the fictional example, your interpretation and any separate evidence a real use would require.
pages.question: Which part of the experience remains an assumption?

pages.title: Keep an alternative beside the favourite.
pages.lead: Compare a dedicated reading corner with a temporary reading session in an existing room. Both are fictional options rather than confirmed plans.
pages.body: An alternative is useful when it tests the same intention under different conditions. Do not turn a preferred image into evidence that the preferred option is feasible.
pages.detail: Use this section to record a bounded response to the question below. Retain the distinction between the fictional example, your interpretation and any separate evidence a real use would require.
pages.question: What would make the alternative worth investigating?

pages.title: Separate responsibilities from appointments.
pages.lead: The concept writer can state the idea, a source reviewer can check evidence and an authorised decision-maker can address a real commitment. These are role categories only.
pages.body: No person has accepted a task through this template. Confirm actual responsibility outside the document before presenting a named owner or a reviewed decision.
pages.detail: Use this section to record a bounded response to the question below. Retain the distinction between the fictional example, your interpretation and any separate evidence a real use would require.
pages.question: Who would need to review a real proposal?

pages.title: Name the missing resource categories.
pages.lead: This example supplies no prices. Venue arrangements, staffing, furniture, maintenance and appropriate reviews remain separate questions.
pages.body: A short list of attractive objects is not a budget. Record unknown categories explicitly rather than inserting invented totals to make the document look finished.
pages.detail: Use this section to record a bounded response to the question below. Retain the distinction between the fictional example, your interpretation and any separate evidence a real use would require.
pages.question: Which omitted cost category could change the discussion?

pages.title: Record the conditions for a next step.
pages.lead: A next conversation could clarify source quality, responsibility and the range of options. It is not permission to purchase, install or operate anything.
pages.body: Use a condition such as obtain relevant site information rather than a promise such as open next month. A condition makes the dependency visible without inventing a schedule.
pages.detail: Use this section to record a bounded response to the question below. Retain the distinction between the fictional example, your interpretation and any separate evidence a real use would require.
pages.question: What must be clarified before commitment?

pages.title: Ask for a bounded response.
pages.lead: Invite a reader to identify a missing source, challenge an assumption or suggest a relevant alternative. Do not ask the document to stand in for formal approval.
pages.body: A useful response identifies the passage being discussed and the kind of evidence needed. Agreeing with an image is not the same as accepting a real project responsibility.
pages.detail: Use this section to record a bounded response to the question below. Retain the distinction between the fictional example, your interpretation and any separate evidence a real use would require.
pages.question: What exact response would improve the next draft?

pages.title: Retain the proposal boundary.
pages.lead: Attach the fictional-source note, current version and unresolved conditions whenever the proposal is shared. The pictures remain illustrations even after the text is edited.
pages.body: A real proposal requires its own verified context and appropriate decision process. This template organises a conversation; it does not certify feasibility, funding or compliance.
